items.title: Anat Cohen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2021
items.q: my classical teacher... her name is Eva Wasserman... she has been very supportive of my path

ctx.x: Would your, I assume you had a classical clarinet teacher early on, and I wonder if they saw you playing on a video, I noticed the one thing I was going to ask you about next, a video with Paquito D’Rivera, and at one point you took, I guess it was your left hand and you put it down at your side while you were playing. Now, and also during this particular solo, you used some lovely vibrato. So I’m wondering if your classical teacher might have looked at that and go oh Anat, you shouldn’t be doing that?

Well my classical teacher, I had one main teacher when I was, before I transformed into jazz life, when I was studying a little bit of classical clarinet and her name is Eva Wasserman, she still lives in Israel. And she has been very supportive of my path and she calls me up and she’s proud of me, and she saw me early on moving away from that strict, strictly classical world and she supported it. And she never made a comment that something is wrong. But it’s always interesting, you know I think years of playing…
That particular moment with the vibrato for some reason made me think of Kenny Davern. You had that particular tone and he’s been a favorite of mine and so I now have another favorite with you.
